reading.text:
UNIT def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Martingale.naturalFiltration -- reading (locked before any Lean)

Paper notion: the natural (raw) filtration of a process W: F^W_t = sigma(W_s : 0 <= s <= t)
(sec. 2: "(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the one generated by W, N and F_0" -- the
filtration generated by a process is its natural filtration). Faithful Lean: a Filtration on the
time index (R_{>=0} or R) with F_t = the supremum over s <= t of the comap sigma-algebras of W_s
(sigma-algebra generated by the random variables W_s, s <= t), for a process W whose values are
measurable (each W_s measurable, so that F_t <= ambient sigma-algebra). Edge cases: s ranging over
[0,t] vs (-oo,t] -- harmless if time is nonnegative; not augmented and not right-continuous (that
is what augFiltration adds); if W_s is not measurable the comap may not lie inside the ambient
sigma-algebra and a Filtration cannot be formed (a junk filtration in that case harmless only if
uses assume measurability).

Paper context (sec. 2, sec. 3, sec. 4, App. A). Standing basis: (Omega,F,(F_t),P) satisfying the usual
conditions, horizon T>0, d-dimensional Brownian motion W and an independent Poisson random
measure N on R_+ x E with intensity dt nu(de), nu sigma-finite on a countably generated (E,E);
(F_t) is the usual augmentation of the filtration generated by W, N and an independent initial
sigma-field F_0. Stochastic integrals int Z dW (Z in H^2_W: R^{m x d}-valued predictable,
E int_0^T |Z|_F^2 dt < oo) and int int U dNtilde (U in H^2_N) are the L^2 (Ito /
compensated-Poisson isometry) integrals; they are true L^2 martingales, cadlag, and are used in
identities holding a.s. for every t (sec. 3, "solution"). The paper never constructs these
integrals itself: it takes the standard construction (Applebaum sec. 4, He-Wang-Yan). So every
unit below is infrastructure: the paper's notion is the textbook one, and a faithful Lean
definition is one that (together with the other definitions) yields the textbook object on the
paper's basis for every integrand the paper's claims use; junk values outside that class are
harmless only if every proposition restricts to the class.

comparison.text:
Comparison: def:LevyStochCalc.Brownian.Martingale.naturalFiltration (Brownian/Martingale.lean:65-70)

Reading: F^W_t = sigma(W_s : 0 <= s <= t), the sup over s <= t of comap(W_s); raw (not augmented,
not right-continuous); s over [0,t] vs (-oo,t] harmless when time is nonnegative.
Lean: MeasureTheory.Filtration.natural W.W (measurability of W_t), i.e. (Mathlib)
seq t := sup_{s <= t} comap (W.W s) (Borel R), as a Filtration R of the ambient sigma-algebra.
Exactly the natural filtration, raw. Representation choice: the time index is R and s ranges over
all reals s <= t, including negative times. BrownianMotion stipulates W_s = 0 a.s. for each s < 0
(negative_zero), so each comap(W_s), s < 0, consists of sets of probability 0 or 1; joining them
changes nothing up to null sets, is invisible after augmentation (augFiltration), and does not
affect independence (the library proves IsBrownianFiltration W (naturalFiltration W) in this
form, isBrownianFiltration_natural).
Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

verdict.detail:
Choice: the filtration is indexed by R and at time t is generated by W_s for all real s <= t,
negative s included. Since W_s = 0 almost surely for each s < 0, the extra generators only add
sets of probability 0 or 1, which are independent of every sigma-algebra and are absorbed by the
null-set augmentation every proposition applies (enlJoint, enlBrownian); W remains a Brownian
motion for it (isBrownianFiltration_natural). On [0, oo) it is sigma(W_s : s <= t) as in the paper.
